claim: Synucleinopathies are characterized by abnormal accumulation of the protein αSyn in the brain.
source: Synucleinopathies are all characterized by abnormal accumulation of the protein αSyn in the brain.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the introduction section of the manuscript.

claim: Synucleinopathies are clinically and neuropathologically highly heterogeneous diseases.
source: However, they are clinically and neuropathologically highly heterogeneous diseases with prominent disease-specific differences in the presentation of symptoms, rate of disease progression, and the brain regions and cell types are vulnerable to αSyn deposition and neuronal death.
evidence: This is stated as an established characteristic of synucleinopathies in the introduction.

claim: In PD, PDD, and DLB, αSyn aggregation is found in the neuronal soma as Lewy bodies (LBs) and in the axons and dendrites as Lewy neurites (LNs).
source: In PD, PDD, and DLB, αSyn aggregation is found in the neuronal soma as Lewy bodies (LBs) and in the axons and dendrites as Lewy neurites (LNs) (Figure 1, Forno, 1988; Spillantini et al., 1997; Braak et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature and reference to Figure 1.

claim: Astroglial accumulation of αSyn is a prominent but underdiagnosed pathology in Lewy body disorders.
source: Furthermore, the astroglial accumulation of αSyn is a prominent but so far underdiagnosed pathology in these Lewy body disorders (Altay et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Altay et al., 2022.

claim: The αSyn pathology in MSA is primarily found in oligodendrocytes as glial cytoplasmic inclusions (GCIs).
source: The αSyn pathology in MSA is primarily found in oligodendrocytes as glial cytoplasmic inclusions (GCIs) (Papp et al., 1989).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Papp et al., 1989.

claim: PD and DLB strains share a 'Lewy fold' structure at the fibrillar core and comprise a single protofilament.
source: At the atomic level, PD and DLB strains share a 'Lewy fold' structure at the fibrillar core and comprise a single protofilament (Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2022 and reference to Figure 1.

claim: MSA strains are twisted with two protofilaments intertwined, forming a different core structure to the 'Lewy fold'.
source: MSA strains are twisted with two protofilaments intertwined, forming a different core structure to the 'Lewy fold' (Schweighauser et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Schweighauser et al., 2020 and reference to Figure 1.

claim: PD is characterized by significant neuronal loss at the brainstem, especially substantia nigra (SN).
source: At a cellular level, PD is characterized by significant neuronal loss at the brainstem, especially substantia nigra (SN), highlighted in blue.
evidence: This is stated in the Figure 1 legend describing the cellular characteristics of PD.

claim: In DLB, the brainstem and neocortex are the most affected regions.
source: In DLB, the brainstem and neocortex are the most affected regions, highlighted in green.
evidence: This is stated in the Figure 1 legend describing the affected regions in DLB.

claim: In MSA, the cerebellum, basal ganglia, and brainstem are the most affected regions.
source: In MSA, the cerebellum, basal ganglia, and brainstem are the most affected, highlighted in red.
evidence: This is stated in the Figure 1 legend describing the affected regions in MSA.

claim: The mechanistic link between αSyn and clinicopathological diversity of synucleinopathies is hypothesized to be different fibrillar 'strains' of αSyn.
source: The mechanistic link between αSyn and clinicopathological diversity of the synucleinopathies is hypothesized to be the different ﬁbrillar 'strains' of αSyn in analogy to prion disease.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the introduction section.

claim: A strain is generated when αSyn monomers fold into specific fibrillar forms with distinct conformational and biological characteristics.
source: A strain is generated when αSyn monomers fold into speciﬁc ﬁbrillar forms with distinct conformational and biological characteristics (Melki, 2018).
evidence: This definition is supported by citation to Melki, 2018.

claim: Under disease conditions, misfolded and aggregated αSyn recruits normal, soluble endogenous αSyn to aggregate in a self-perpetuating process that spreads throughout the brain-periphery axis.
source: Under the disease condition, misfolded and aggregated αSyn recruits normal, soluble endogenous αSyn to aggregate, and this self-perpetuating process spreads throughout the brain-periphery axis.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of αSyn propagation based on established knowledge.

claim: Human-derived αSyn strains exhibit distinct structures.
source: However, some studies have also examined αSyn fibrils extracted from the human brain tissue of different synucleinopathies and these have demonstrated that the human-derived αSyn strains exhibit distinct structures (Schweighauser et al., 2020), infectivity and bioactivity in cells (Woerman et al., 2018a; Woerman et al., 2019; Ayers et al., 2022) and animals (Prusiner et al., 2015; Lau et al., 2020; Holec et al., 2022; Peng et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior studies.

claim: Human-derived αSyn strains exhibit distinct infectivity and bioactivity in cells.
source: However, some studies have also examined αSyn fibrils extracted from the human brain tissue of different synucleinopathies and these have demonstrated that the human-derived αSyn strains exhibit distinct structures (Schweighauser et al., 2020), infectivity and bioactivity in cells (Woerman et al., 2018a; Woerman et al., 2019; Ayers et al., 2022) and animals (Prusiner et al., 2015; Lau et al., 2020; Holec et al., 2022; Peng et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Woerman et al., 2018a; Woerman et al., 2019; Ayers et al., 2022.

claim: Human-derived αSyn strains exhibit distinct infectivity and bioactivity in animals.
source: However, some studies have also examined αSyn fibrils extracted from the human brain tissue of different synucleinopathies and these have demonstrated that the human-derived αSyn strains exhibit distinct structures (Schweighauser et al., 2020), infectivity and bioactivity in cells (Woerman et al., 2018a; Woerman et al., 2019; Ayers et al., 2022) and animals (Prusiner et al., 2015; Lau et al., 2020; Holec et al., 2022; Peng et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Prusiner et al., 2015; Lau et al., 2020; Holec et al., 2022; Peng et al., 2018.

claim: The intrinsic structure of αSyn proteoforms may depend on the local conditions of the brain region where they are formed and may vary within a single disease entity.
source: The intrinsic structure of αSyn proteoforms may also depend on the local conditions of the brain region where they are formed and thus may vary within a single disease entity (Peng et al., 2018; Lau et al., 2020; Schweighauser et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Peng et al., 2018; Lau et al., 2020; Schweighauser et al., 2020.

claim: SAA refers to two distinct seed amplification techniques: real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) and protein misfolding cyclic amplification (PMCA).
source: SAA refers to two distinct seed amplification techniques: real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) and protein misfolding cyclic amplification (PMCA).
evidence: This is a definition provided in the introduction.

claim: Both RT-QuIC and PMCA incorporate the ability of pathological αSyn to induce aggregation of monomeric αSyn into different complex conformers.
source: Both methods incorporate a key characteristic of pathological αSyn, which is its ability to induce aggregation of monomeric αSyn into different complex conformers.
evidence: This describes the common principle underlying both SAA methods.

claim: When pathological αSyn is present in the biosample, it seeds aggregation of recombinant αSyn through repeated elongation-fragmentation cycles.
source: When pathological αSyn is present in the biosample, it seeds aggregation of the recombinant αSyn in the reaction through repeated elongation-fragmentation cycles (Concha-Marambio et al., 2023).
evidence: This mechanism is supported by citation to Concha-Marambio et al., 2023.

claim: RT-QuIC uses physical shaking for aggregate fragmentation, while PMCA uses sonication.
source: A major difference between the two methods lies in the method of aggregate fragmentation (Coysh and Mead, 2022). RT-QuIC uses physical shaking, and PMCA uses sonication.
evidence: This difference is stated and supported by citation to Coysh and Mead, 2022.

claim: RT-QuIC reaction is monitored automatically in real-time using a fluorophore such as Thioflavin-T (ThT), whereas PMCA requires manual measurement.
source: Also, the RT-QuIC reaction is monitored automatically in real-time using a fluorophore such as Thioflavin-T (ThT), whereas PMCA requires manual measurement.
evidence: This describes a methodological difference between RT-QuIC and PMCA.

claim: RT-QuIC products are not infectious, while PMCA produces infectious aggregates with specific strain fidelity.
source: Furthermore, it should be noted that the RT-QuIC products are not infectious, while the PMCA produces infectious aggregates with specific strain fidelity (Raymond et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Raymond et al., 2020.

claim: SAA has potential as a diagnostic method using different biosamples such as cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), brain homogenates, and skin punctures.
source: SAA, together with different biosamples such as cerebrospinal ﬂuid (CSF) (Fairfoul et al., 2016; Poggiolini et al., 2022), brain homogenates (Groveman et al., 2018; Sano et al., 2018), and skin punctures (Mammana et al., 2020; Kuzkina et al., 2021), has presented its potential as a diagnostic method but also as a research tool to amplify disease-relevant ﬁbrils.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior studies.

claim: SAA fibrils are assumed to encode the intrinsic properties of the original seeding fibrils.
source: The newly ampliﬁed SAA ﬁbrils are assumed to encode the intrinsic properties of the original seeding fibrils, thus being representative of the disease-speciﬁc strains.
evidence: This is stated as an assumption underlying the use of SAA fibrils.

claim: Studies using SAA fibrils have shown disease-specific structural, biochemical, and phenotypic differences, suggesting the presence of distinct conformational αSyn strains in different synucleinopathies.
source: Therefore, using the 'model' SAA ﬁbrils, studies have shown disease-speciﬁc structural, biochemical, and phenotypic differences, suggesting the presence of distinct conformational αSyn strains in different synucleinopathies (Strohäker et al., 2019; Shahnawaz et al., 2020; Van der Perren et al., 2020; Frieg et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Strohäker et al., 2019; Shahnawaz et al., 2020; Van der Perren et al., 2020; Frieg et al., 2022.

claim: Studies have highlighted significant structural differences between human brain-derived and SAA fibrils.
source: Despite such extensive strain characterisation performed with the SAA fibrils, whether the SAA fibrils are representative models of the original seed fibrils is unclear. Studies highlighted the significant structural differences between the human brain-derived and SAA ﬁbrils (Lövestam et al., 2021) and seeded pathology in vivo (Van der Perren et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lövestam et al., 2021 and Van der Perren et al., 2020.

claim: There is limited understanding of whether SAA fibrils preserve properties including biochemical, biophysical, cellular toxicity, and pathology of the original seed fibrils.
source: Nevertheless, there is currently a limited understanding of whether the resulting SAA ﬁbrils preserve other properties, including biochemical, biophysical, cellular toxicity, and pathology.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current knowledge.

claim: PD, PDD, DLB, and MSA brain-derived αSyn fibrils reached maximum ThT fluorescence within 100 hr in SAA reactions.
source: PD, PDD, DLB, and MSA brain-derived αSyn fibrils reached the maximum ThT fluorescence within 100 hr (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the SAA experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Healthy control samples did not display seeding potential except for case 2 (HC 2), which showed an increasing signal towards the end of the reaction at approximately 91 hr.
source: The healthy controls did not display seeding potential except for case 2 (HC 2), which showed an increasing signal towards the end of the reaction (approximately 91 hr) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the SAA experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Unseeded recombinant αSyn remained negative in all SAA reactions.
source: The unseeded recombinant αSyn remained negative in all reactions (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a control observation from the SAA experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The area under the curve (AUC) was statistically higher in PDD/DLB than in PD/MSA.
source: As a result, the area under the curve (AUC) was statistically higher in PDD/DLB than in PD/MSA (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the kinetic analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: PDD and DLB brain-derived αSyn fibrils have a more aggressive seeding capacity than PD and MSA.
source: Overall, the SAA kinetic parameters suggest PDD and DLB brain-derived αSyn fibrils have a more aggressive seeding capacity than PD and MSA.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the kinetic data presented in Figure 2.

claim: The weakest GdnHCl (1 M) treatment completely denatured PD and MSA brain-derived αSyn fibrils.
source: The weakest GdnHCl (1 M) treatment completely denatured the PD and MSA brain-derived αSyn fibrils, as they were no longer visible on the immunoblot (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the biochemical stability assay shown in Figure 3.

claim: Higher GdnHCl concentrations of 2 M and 3 M denatured PDD and DLB brain-derived αSyn fibrils, respectively.
source: Higher GdnHCl concentrations of 2 M and 3 M denatured PDD and DLB brain-derived αSyn fibrils, respectively (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the biochemical stability assay shown in Figure 3.

claim: PD and MSA brain-derived αSyn fibrils have weaker biochemical stability than PDD and DLB fibrils.
source: The results illustrate that PD and MSA brain-derived αSyn fibrils have weaker biochemical stability than PDD and DLB fibrils.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GdnHCl denaturation data shown in Figure 3.

claim: PD cases contained mostly monomeric αSyn (15 kDa) that immediately degraded at the lowest PK concentration (1 ug/ml).
source: PD cases contained mostly monomeric αSyn (15 kDa) that immediately degraded at the lowest PK concentration (1 ug/ml) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the PK digestion assay shown in Figure 4A.

claim: In PDD, DLB, and MSA cases, high molecular weight (MW) bands above 15 kDa were observed, indicative of αSyn aggregates.
source: In contrast, in PDD, DLB, and MSA cases, high molecular weight (MW) bands above 15 kDa were observed, indicative of αSyn aggregates (Figure 4B–D).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the PK digestion assay shown in Figure 4B-D.

claim: Lower MW bands (13, 10, 7 kDa) were observed in PDD, DLB, and MSA cases.
source: Furthermore, lower MW bands (13, 10, 7 kDa) were also observed.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the PK digestion assay.

claim: PDD and DLB fibrils gradually degraded as PK concentration increased, with high MW bands disappearing and low MW bands appearing.
source: As the PK concentration increased, the PDD and DLB fibrils gradually degraded, as the high MW bands started to disappear and low MW bands below 15 kDa began to appear (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the PK digestion assay shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: MSA fibrils gradually degraded as PK concentration increased, but low MW bands below 15 kDa were less prominent than those of PDD and DLB.
source: Similarly, the MSA fibrils gradually degraded as the PK concentration increased (Figure 4D). However, low MW bands below 15 kDa were less prominent than those of PDD and DLB.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the PK digestion assay shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Low MW bands were absent in healthy controls (HC).
source: These low MW bands were absent in HC (Figure 4E), and PD and HC showed no difference in the PK profiles.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the PK digestion assay shown in Figure 4E.

claim: PD and HC showed no difference in the PK profiles.
source: These low MW bands were absent in HC (Figure 4E), and PD and HC showed no difference in the PK profiles.
evidence: This is a direct observation from comparing PK digestion profiles.

claim: PDD brains showed higher LB load in the entorhinal cortex compared to PD brains.
source: Using immunohistochemistry, we observed a lower load of αSyn pathology in PD and MSA brains than in PDD and DLB (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: PD and MSA cases contained 1–3 αSyn fibrils per region of interest (ROI) in TEM imaging.
source: PD and MSA cases contained 1–3 αSyn ﬁbrils per region of interest (ROI), whereas PDD and DLB cases contained 3–5 αSyn ﬁbrils per ROI (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from TEM imaging shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: PDD and DLB cases contained 3–5 αSyn fibrils per region of interest (ROI) in TEM imaging.
source: PD and MSA cases contained 1–3 αSyn ﬁbrils per region of interest (ROI), whereas PDD and DLB cases contained 3–5 αSyn ﬁbrils per ROI (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from TEM imaging shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Slot blots confirmed a higher amount of αSyn fibrils in PDD and DLB than in PD and MSA brain-derived samples.
source: Adjacent slot blots also conﬁrmed a higher amount of αSyn ﬁbrils in PDD and DLB than in PD and MSA brain-derived samples.
evidence: This is a direct observation from slot blot analysis.

claim: Lower fibril concentration in PD and MSA brains could have limited the observation of PK-resistant peptides using immunoblotting.
source: Therefore, lower ﬁbril concentration in the PD and MSA brains could have limited the observation of the PK-resistant peptides using immunoblotting.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed differences in fibril concentration.

claim: SAA fibrils revealed markedly different biochemical profiles to the brain-derived αSyn fibrils.
source: The SAA ﬁbrils revealed markedly different biochemical proﬁles to the brain-derived αSyn ﬁbrils.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the biochemical comparison between brain-derived and SAA fibrils.

claim: Identical biochemical profiles were observed among all SAA fibrils from PD, PDD, DLB, and MSA.
source: We observed identical proﬁles among all SAA ﬁbrils from PD, PDD, DLB, and MSA.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the biochemical analysis of SAA fibrils.

claim: PK-resistant bands of 7 and 10 kDa started to appear in SAA fibrils after treatment with 2 M GdnHCl.
source: PK-resistant bands of 7 and 10 kDa started to appear after treatment with 2 M GdnHCl (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the biochemical stability assay shown in Figure 3.

claim: With increasing concentrations of GdnHCl, specific PK-resistant peptides appeared in SAA fibrils, consisting of five bands (7, 11, 12, 13, 14 kDa).
source: However, with increasing concentrations of GdnHCl, speciﬁc PK-resistant peptides appeared, consisting of ﬁve bands (7, 11, 12, 13, 14 kDa) (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the biochemical stability assay shown in Figure 3.

claim: Harsher denaturing conditions are required to destabilize SAA fibrils and expose PK digestion sites.
source: These ﬁndings suggest that harsher denaturing conditions are required to destabilize the SAA ﬁbrils and expose PK digestion sites.
evidence: This is an inference based on the GdnHCl and PK treatment results.

claim: SAA αSyn fibrils are more stable and characterized by distinct biochemical properties than the brain-derived αSyn fibrils.
source: We concluded that SAA αSyn ﬁbrils are more stable and characterized by distinct biochemical properties than the brain-derived αSyn ﬁbrils.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the biochemical stability and PK resistance data.

claim: Brain-derived αSyn fibrils from PD, PDD, and DLB exhibited two structures in TEM: straight and twisted.
source: The brain-derived αSyn ﬁbrils from PD, PDD, and DLB exhibited two structures in TEM: straight and twisted (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from TEM imaging shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Brain-derived fibrils from MSA were predominantly straight, with rare presence of twisted type.
source: The ﬁbrils from MSA were predominantly straight, with the rare presence of twisted type.
evidence: This is a direct observation from TEM imaging.

claim: The length of brain-derived fibrils from different synucleinopathies ranged between 68–885 nm.
source: The length of the ﬁbrils from different synucleinopathies ranged between 68–885 nm.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from TEM analysis.

claim: PDD brain-derived fibrils were significantly longer than DLB and MSA fibrils.
source: Only the PDD ﬁbrils were signiﬁcantly longer than DLB and MSA (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the fibril dimension analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The width of brain-derived fibrils ranged from 7 to 21 nm, with significant differences between diseases.
source: The width ranged from 7 to 21 nm, and there were significant differences between the diseases.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from TEM analysis.

claim: PD had the widest brain-derived fibrils, followed by MSA/DLB and PDD.
source: PD had the widest ﬁbrils, followed by MSA/DLB and PDD (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the fibril dimension analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: PD, PDD, and DLB SAA fibrils were all straight.
source: On the other hand, the SAA ﬁbrils demonstrated a single dominant structure. PD, PDD, and DLB SAA ﬁbrils were all straight, and MSA SAA ﬁbrils were all twisted (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from TEM imaging shown in Figure 5A.

claim: MSA SAA fibrils were all twisted.
source: On the other hand, the SAA ﬁbrils demonstrated a single dominant structure. PD, PDD, and DLB SAA ﬁbrils were all straight, and MSA SAA ﬁbrils were all twisted (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from TEM imaging shown in Figure 5A.

claim: SAA fibrils were highly clustered, unlike brain-derived fibrils.
source: Unlike the brain-derived ﬁbrils, the SAA ﬁbrils were highly clustered.
evidence: This is a direct observation from TEM imaging.

claim: The length of SAA fibrils ranged from 104 to 1008 nm.
source: The length of the SAA ﬁbrils ranged from 104 to 1008 nm, and PDD/DLB SAA ﬁbrils were signiﬁcantly longer than those of PD/MSA (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from TEM analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: PDD/DLB SAA fibrils were significantly longer than those of PD/MSA.
source: The length of the SAA ﬁbrils ranged from 104 to 1008 nm, and PDD/DLB SAA ﬁbrils were signiﬁcantly longer than those of PD/MSA (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the fibril dimension analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The width of SAA fibrils ranged from 8 to 25 nm.
source: The width ranged from 8 to 25 nm, and the widths of the MSA SAA ﬁbrils were distributed into two groups due to the alternating widths arising from the twisted structure.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from TEM analysis.

claim: The widths of MSA SAA fibrils were distributed into two groups due to the alternating widths arising from the twisted structure.
source: The width ranged from 8 to 25 nm, and the widths of the MSA SAA ﬁbrils were distributed into two groups due to the alternating widths arising from the twisted structure.
evidence: This is an observation and interpretation from TEM analysis.

claim: The average widths of SAA fibrils were similar between different synucleinopathies.
source: Unlike the brain-derived ﬁbrils, the average widths of the SAA ﬁbrils were similar between different synucleinopathies (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the fibril dimension analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: In DLB, SAA fibrils were significantly longer and wider than brain-derived fibrils.
source: Overall, in DLB, the SAA ﬁbrils were signiﬁcantly longer and wider than the brain-derived ﬁbrils (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the comparative analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: SAA fibrils from PDD were wider than brain-derived fibrils but not different in length.
source: SAA ﬁbrils from PDD were wider than the brain-derived ﬁbrils but not different in length.
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the comparative analysis.

claim: The dimensions of brain-derived and SAA fibrils from PD and MSA were not significantly different.
source: The dimensions of the brain-derived and SAA ﬁbrils from PD and MSA were not significantly different.
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the comparative analysis.

claim: Brain-derived and SAA αSyn fibrils exhibit distinct TEM structures.
source: Our observations demonstrate that brain-derived and SAA αSyn ﬁbrils exhibit distinct TEM structures.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TEM structural analysis.

claim: Both brain-derived and SAA fibrils from all four synucleinopathies were probed with MJFR-14, confirming that the fibrils were αSyn fibrils.
source: Both brain-derived and SAA ﬁbrils from all four synucleinopathies were probed with MJFR-14, conﬁrming that the ﬁbrils were αSyn ﬁbrils (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from immunogold labeling shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Brain-derived fibrils were strongly labeled with anti-pαSyn.
source: The brain-derived ﬁbrils were also strongly labeled with anti-pαSyn.
evidence: This is a direct observation from immunogold labeling.

claim: MJFR-14 and anti-pαSyn antibodies did not label the twisted brain-derived fibrils from PD, PDD, and DLB.
source: Both antibodies, however, did not label the twisted brain-derived ﬁbrils from PD, PDD, and DLB (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from immunogold labeling shown in Figure 6B.

claim: SAA fibrils from PD and MSA were not labeled with anti-pαSyn.
source: The SAA ﬁbrils from PD and MSA were not labeled with anti-pαSyn, but PD and MSA SAA ﬁbrils were weakly labeled (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from immunogold labeling shown in Figure 6A. Note: There appears to be a typo in the manuscript text ('PD and MSA' should likely be 'PDD and DLB' based on context).

claim: PDD and DLB SAA fibrils were weakly labeled with anti-pαSyn.
source: The SAA ﬁbrils from PD and MSA were not labeled with anti-pαSyn, but PD and MSA SAA ﬁbrils were weakly labeled (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is inferred from the context and Figure 6A, as the text appears to contain a typo.

claim: DLB brain-derived αSyn fibrils showed the strongest signal with MJFR-14 and anti-pαSyn on slot blot, followed by PDD, MSA, and PD.
source: On the slot blot, DLB brain-derived αSyn ﬁbrils showed the strongest signal with MJFR-14 and anti-pαSyn, followed by PDD, MSA, and PD (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from slot blot analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: PDD SAA fibrils showed the highest anti-pαSyn signal among SAA fibrils.
source: In parallel to the anti-pαSyn immunogold results (Figure 6A), PDD SAA ﬁbrils showed the highest anti-pαSyn signal (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a direct observation from slot blot analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: DLB SAA fibrils were weakly phosphorylated.
source: The DLB SAA ﬁbrils were also weakly phosphorylated, while those of PD and MSA were negative.
evidence: This is a direct observation from slot blot analysis.

claim: PD and MSA SAA fibrils were negative for phosphorylation.
source: The DLB SAA ﬁbrils were also weakly phosphorylated, while those of PD and MSA were negative.
evidence: This is a direct observation from slot blot analysis.

claim: Phosphorylated αSyn in SAA fibrils must have transmitted from the seed brain-derived fibrils, given the absence of phosphorylated recombinant monomers in the SAA reaction.
source: Considering the absence of phosphorylated recombinant monomers in our SAA reaction, the phosphorylated αSyn must have transmitted from the seed brain-derived fibrils.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental design and phosphorylation observations.

claim: Brain-derived and SAA αSyn fibrils display different patterns of S129 phosphorylation.
source: Our results demonstrate that the brain-derived and SAA αSyn ﬁbrils display different patterns of S129 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the phosphorylation analysis.

claim: Faster seeding kinetics were observed in brain-derived αSyn fibrils from PDD and DLB than those from PD and MSA, suggesting a distinct 'strain' characterized by aggressive seeding capacity.
source: First, faster seeding kinetics were observed in the brain-derived αSyn ﬁbrils from PDD and DLB than those from PD and MSA, suggesting a distinct 'strain' characterized by an aggressive seeding capacity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the seeding kinetics data.

claim: PD and MSA brain-derived fibrils represent discrete 'strains' with milder seeding capacity.
source: In contrast, those from PD and MSA are discrete 'strains' with milder seeding capacity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the seeding kinetics data.

claim: PDD cases had longer disease duration than PD, although both shared the same Braak stage 6.
source: In particular, our PDD cases had longer disease duration than PD, although both shared the same Braak stage 6.
evidence: This is stated as a consideration when analyzing seeding kinetics.

claim: The Braak staging only represents the distribution of LB pathology and fails to consider the load of LBs.
source: The Braak staging, however, only represents the distribution of LB pathology and fails to consider the load of LBs.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the Braak staging system.

claim: A higher accumulation of fibrils in PDD brains might have resulted in faster seeding kinetics.
source: Thus, a higher accumulation of fibrils in PDD brains might have resulted in faster seeding kinetics.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed differences in fibril load.

claim: DLB cases had shorter disease duration than PDD but comparable burden of LBs and similar seeding kinetics.
source: Nevertheless, our DLB cases had shorter disease duration than PDD, but the comparable burden of LBs and both diseases demonstrated similar seeding kinetics.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study data.

claim: Differential seeding kinetics is likely to result from strain properties or burden of pathology rather than disease duration.
source: Thus, the differential seeding kinetics is likely to result from strain properties or burden of pathology rather than disease duration.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of disease duration, pathology burden, and seeding kinetics.

claim: In αSyn SAA with brain-derived fibrils, the same parameters (T50, VMAX) cannot distinguish between PD and MSA.
source: However, in our αSyn SAA with brain-derived ﬁbrils, the same parameters cannot distinguish between PD and MSA.
evidence: This is a direct finding from the study's SAA experiments.

claim: Differences in SAA findings between CSF and brain-derived fibrils are likely to arise from the type of seeds.
source: Differences in the ﬁndings are likely to arise from the type of seeds.
